title: Competitive Topology: Mapping Model Adoption Pathways and Enterprise Friction Points
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Create a bounded, evidence-driven map of how enterprises discover, evaluate, and adopt third-party LLM providers (hosted, dedicated, private). The artifact will identify decision pivots (latency, cost, compliance, vendor lock), typical buyer personas, and the friction points that cause customers to prefer Redwood Inference or consider alternatives.
background: PMs and sales frequently request a prescriptive view of buyer journeys for model procurement and migration. Existing landscape docs enumerate suppliers and capabilities but lack structured adoption pathways and explicit friction triggers that engineering and solutions teams can act on. This ticket delivers a consolidated topology artifact and a prioritized research sprint to validate hypotheses with field evidence.
goals: Produce a topology diagram showing discovery -> evaluation -> proof-of-concept -> procurement -> rollout stages for enterprise LLM adoption
Identify top 6 friction triggers that push customers toward Dedicated/Private deployments (e.g., data residency, latency SLOs, compliance audits)
Provide 10 evidence-backed buyer persona profiles (engineer, ML platform, security/compliance, procurement)
Deliver prioritized go-to-research tasks and sample prompts for sales enablement and solution templates
tasks: Synthesize prior model-landscape research into a first-draft topology (artifact: /drive/ModelTopology/Draft-v1.pdf)
Interview 6 customer-facing stakeholders (AE, SE, CS) and capture decision anecdotes (use research form: https://forms.gle/redwood-research-topology)
Run telemetry slice: identify 100 customers who moved from Hosted -> Dedicated and extract motivators from onboarding notes (dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/telemetry/migration-trace)
Map competitor touchpoints by analyzing public docs and SLA pages for top 8 providers (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/competitive-monitor)
Validate 3 highest-risk friction hypotheses with 2 enterprise customers each (coordinate with Solutions Engineering for intro)
Produce final topology deliverable and an executive 1-pager for GTM and AE playbooks
acceptance_criteria: Topology diagram exists as a shareable PDF and editable Miro board link
At least 6 interviews logged and summarized in the research spreadsheet
A prioritization table that links friction triggers to product levers (batching, routing, private deploy, SLAs) is completed
Hand-off to GTM with 1 AE enablement call and a slide deck approved by head of Sales
notes: Trade-off: we should avoid overfitting the topology to hyper-specific verticals; focus on cross-vertical decision pivots first
Kernel scheduling / runtime arguments are expected to be a recurring 'engineering blocker' motif in interviews; loop in runtime lead early
Data residency emerges often as a procurement-level blocker; investigate recent Private deployment case studies for concrete timelines and cost tradeoffs
